title: Classic Roast Beef Sirloin
description: Sunday-lunch staple. A 1.5kg sirloin joint rested off the bone with a simple herb crust. Serve with the lemon-herb potatoes and a red-wine gravy.

steps.text: Pre-heat oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Take the joint out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking to come to room temperature.
Pat the joint dry with kitchen paper. Rub all over with olive oil, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear in a hot, dry pan on every side until deeply browned — about 6 minutes total. This is your crust.
Transfer to a roasting tin. Scatter thyme and crushed garlic over the top. Roast for 20 minutes per 500g for medium-rare (so ~60 minutes for this joint).
Rest covered loosely with foil for at least 20 minutes before carving. The internal temp will climb 3-4°C off the heat.
Carve against the grain into 0.5cm slices. Serve with the rendered pan juices spooned over.

title: Vegan Mushroom Risotto
description: Wild mushroom risotto finished with nutritional yeast for a parmesan-like depth. Vegan, gluten-free if the stock is.

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan, fry the mushrooms in batches until golden and any liquid has evaporated. Set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cook 1 minute more.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring. Pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often. Wait until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. Takes ~18 minutes total.
When the rice is just tender with a slight bite, stir in the mushrooms and nutritional yeast. Season generously.
Rest off the heat for 2 minutes. Serve in warm bowls with a final drizzle of olive oil and cracked pepper.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon Butter
description: Crisp-skinned salmon fillet with a quick lemon butter pan sauce. 12 minutes start to plate.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry. Score the skin if thick. Season both sides with salt.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Place the fillets skin-side down and press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds so the skin stays flat.
Cook skin-side down for 5-6 minutes until the skin is deep gold and crisp. The flesh should look cooked 75% of the way up the fillet.
Flip, cook for 1-2 minutes more depending on thickness. Transfer to plates skin-up.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add butter, lemon juice, zest, and capers. Swirl until the butter has melted into a glossy sauce.
Spoon the sauce around (not over) the salmon to keep the skin crisp. Finish with parsley.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, charred under the grill, then folded into a smoky tomato + cream sauce. Serve with basmati and naan.

steps.text: Mix the chicken with yoghurt, 2 tbsp garam masala, half the garlic and half the ginger. Marinate at least 30 minutes (overnight is better).
Thread onto skewers (or spread on a tray). Grill under high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning once, until edges are charred. Set aside.
In a heavy pan, sweat the onion in oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add remaining garlic, ginger, and garam masala. Cook 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Simmer 15 minutes until reduced and glossy. Blend smooth with a stick blender if you prefer a clean sauce.
Stir in the cream + grilled chicken. Simmer 5 more minutes for the flavours to come together. Season with salt.
Serve over hot basmati rice with naan and fresh coriander.

title: Classic Caesar Salad
description: Crisp baby gem, anchovy-rich dressing, parmesan shavings, garlic croutons. Real Caesar — the way the original Tijuana Hotel served it.

ingredients.name: Parmesan, finely grated + shaved for garnish

steps.text: Pre-heat oven to 200°C. Toss the torn sourdough with 2 tbsp olive oil + 1 clove crushed garlic. Bake on a tray for 8 minutes until crisp.
In a bowl, mash 4 anchovies and the remaining garlic to a paste. Whisk in the egg yolks.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking, as for mayonnaise, until thick and emulsified.
Whisk in the lemon juice + grated parmesan. Season with salt + pepper. Taste — it should be punchy and savoury.
Toss the lettuce leaves with the dressing in a wide bowl until every leaf is coated.
Plate with croutons scattered through, top with parmesan shavings + remaining anchovy fillets.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
description: Individual molten-centre chocolate cakes. 12 minutes in the oven, runny middle guaranteed if you don't overbake.

steps.text: Pre-heat oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Generously butter 4 × 200ml dariole moulds and dust with cocoa powder.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over barely-simmering water. Stir until smooth, then cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, yolks, and sugar until pale and thickened (about 3 minutes with electric beaters).
Fold the chocolate mixture into the eggs, then sift in the flour and fold gently. Don't overmix.
Divide between the moulds. Bake for exactly 12 minutes — the tops should be set but the centre still wobbly.
Rest for 1 minute, then turn out onto plates. Dust with cocoa and serve immediately with cream or ice cream.

title: Lemon Herb Roast Potatoes
description: Crispy on the outside, fluffy inside. Maris Piper or King Edward potatoes parboiled then roasted in olive oil with lemon zest and rosemary.

ingredients.name: Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and quartered

steps.text: Pre-heat oven to 220°C / fan 200°C. Pour the olive oil into a large roasting tray and slide into the oven to heat up.
Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 8 minutes until just yielding to a knife tip. Drain and shake them in the colander to rough up the edges.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil — they should sizzle. Turn each one with a spoon to coat. Roast for 30 minutes.
Turn the potatoes, scatter over the garlic cloves and rosemary. Return to the oven for 15-20 more minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Sprinkle with sea salt and the lemon zest while still hot. Serve immediately.

title: Quick Tomato Pasta
description: A weeknight pasta in under 20 minutes. Good tinned San Marzano tomatoes, garlic, fresh basil, generous black pepper.

steps.text: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Drop in the spaghetti.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the sliced garlic — let it gently turn pale gold (don't burn it).
Crush the tinned tomatoes by hand into the pan. Add the chilli flakes. Simmer 8 minutes until thickened.
When the pasta is 1 minute shy of al dente, lift it directly into the sauce with tongs, bringing a splash of pasta water with it.
Toss vigorously over the heat for 1 minute. The starchy water emulsifies the sauce around the strands.
Tear the basil leaves over. Plate, finish with a final drizzle of olive oil and cracked pepper.
